subject: Committed Spend: proposed shelf drawdown + early-burn trigger
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@acmeai.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmeai.com>, Tim Chen <tim.chen@acmeai.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood commitment question — shelf drawdown options

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We liked the latency and predictability profile. Procurement asked me to surface one item before we move to term-sheet: how would a multi-year committed prepay work if we want an annual wallet that draws down but allows an early-burn trigger (i.e., if we exceed a specified monthly threshold, the wallet pulls forward and offers an acceleration credit)?

High-level constraints from our side:
- 3-year term preferred but flexible on 2 vs 3
- Prefer annual wallets for bookkeeping (yearly buckets)
- Need reconciliation monthly with true-up to actual usage
- Want a clear formula for early-burn acceleration and a limit on how much can be accelerated per month

Can you share a sketch of how Redwood typically structures this? Also, any specific billing/recognition implications we should flag for our finance team?

Appreciate it —
Elena
Elena Park
Head of Platform Partnerships | AcmeAI
Attachments: acme_usage_profile_q1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@acmeai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood commitment question — shelf drawdown options

Elena —

Thanks for the clear constraints. Below is a concise sketch of one approach we use that matches what you described (we can adjust parameters):

Proposed structure (sketch):
- Term: 3 years with annual wallets (Year 1 / Year 2 / Year 3) funded up front or on anniversary.
- Drawdown: Usage is charged against the current year wallet first. If month-to-month usage exceeds a pre-defined threshold (early-burn trigger), the system auto-draws from the next year’s wallet up to a capped % (suggest 20% of next-year wallet per month).
- Acceleration credit: For draws pulled forward because of early-burn, we apply an acceleration credit of X% (negotiable) relative to standard per-token price to compensate forecast variance.
- True-up: Monthly reconciliation with overage billed or credited at the agreed committed rate; unused prepay at year-end can be reallocated/forfeited depending on clause (we recommend a 6-month reallocation window).
- Billing & recognition: For your finance team, prepay is recognized as deferred revenue on Redwood side and consumed monthly; we can provide monthly usage statements and GL-friendly export.

I attached a draft term sheet with the above as placeholders. Happy to run numbers with your usage file.

Next steps: 1) Ben (cc) will run model scenarios on the attached usage profile; 2) Marissa will flag any accounting/recognition questions for her team; 3) Logan/Ben to propose % caps and acceleration credit bands by end of day Friday.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_Commitment_Termsheet_v3.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@acmeai.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Redwood commitment question — shelf drawdown options

Looping in some quick modeled outcomes based on Acme's Q1 file. Summary first, details inline:

Summary (model highlights):
- Base committed rate: $0.0035 / token (placeholder) with tiered discounts by annual wallet size.
- Proposed early-burn cap: 18% of next-year wallet per month (keeps runway but allows spike absorption).
- Acceleration credit: 12% applied to the drawn-forward portion for months where trigger fires. This effectively reduces the per-token rate on accelerated drawdown.
- Expected cashflow: front-loaded (if funded up front) or staged on anniversaries. Up-front prepay improves unit economics (deeper discount).

Detailed notes:
- If Acme chooses up-front funding for all three years we can offer an incremental 5% term discount. If they prefer annual funding on anniversary, discount steps down ~2% per deferred year.
- Reconciliation: monthly usage vs wallet consumption; overage beyond wallets billed at committed spot with 30-day invoice terms.
- For accounting: Marissa, the main ask is whether Redwood can provide an itemized CSV with monthly consumption and deferred revenue balance for Acme's auditors. We can commit to that.

I'll attach the scenario workbook in a follow-up (sized for three ramp profiles).

-ben
Ben Carter
Principal Sales Ops | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@acmeai.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Mar 2027 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Redwood commitment question — shelf drawdown options

Elena —

A couple of accounting points from our side to flag early:
- If Acme prepays for an annual wallet we will classify cash received as deferred revenue and recognize monthly as usage is consumed. We can provide monthly GL exports and a year-end summary for audits.
- For acceleration (draws pulled from future wallets), we treat the draw as consumption against that future deferred balance — recognition follows consumption timing. The acceleration credit is a pricing adjustment (we'll show it as a discount line item).
- Contract clause request: to support reallocation, suggest a 6-month window after each anniversary where unused wallet amounts can be reallocated to other Redwood products or rolled forward subject to cap.

If you want, Priyom (cc) can draft the specific contract language around the early-burn cap and reallocation windows to speed legal review.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Finance, Revenue | Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@acmeai.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Mar 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft clause: early-burn acceleration & reallocation (for review)

Elena / Team —

Draft language below that we can drop into the term sheet. Happy to iterate:

"Early-burn accelerator and reallocation: If Customer's monthly consumption exceeds the Early-Burn Threshold (defined as 120% of the Customer's modeled monthly baseline), Redwood may automatically draw funds from the succeeding Year's Wallet for the purpose of covering such overage, up to a maximum of 18% of the succeeding Year's Wallet per calendar month. Amounts drawn forward under this clause shall receive an Acceleration Credit of 12% (twelve percent) applied to the per-unit committed rate. Unused funds at the end of a Contract Year may be reallocated within six (6) months to other Redwood products or rolled forward to the next Contract Year, subject to a maximum rollforward cap equal to 25% of the original Wallet amount for that Contract Year."

Key negotiation levers remaining: threshold % (120% baseline), monthly cap (18%), acceleration credit (12%), reallocation window (6 months), rollforward cap (25%).

If this aligns with Acme's expectation we'll update the term sheet and deliver a redline.

-priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Park <elena.park@acmeai.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmeai.com>, Tim Chen <tim.chen@acmeai.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 22:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Redwood commitment question — shelf drawdown options

Thanks — this is really helpful and mostly aligns with what Procurement needs. A few quick counterpoints from Acme:
- We'd like a slightly higher monthly cap on draw-forward for the first 6 months of the relationship (30%) to absorb expected onboarding spikes. After six months cap should revert to 18%.
- Acceleration credit: can we push to 15% for the drawn portion in Year 1 only if we fund Year 1 up-front?
- Reallocation: 6 months is OK, but can you add language that unused funds can be returned (less a minimal admin fee) if we terminate for convenience at the end of Year 1?

If you can update the draft clause with those options we'll take it back to procurement and legal for a final pass. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Best,
Elena Park
Head of Platform Partnerships | AcmeAI
